s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss with intraocular hemorrhage and crystalline deposits
salient_findings: Spontaneous hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage in one eye
Presence of glistening crystals in the anterior chamber
Iridescent, needle-like crystals floating in the aqueous
key_facts: Patient is a young girl
Right eye is blind
Hyphema and vitreous hemorrhage occurred spontaneously
Multiple glistening crystals were observed in the anterior chamber
Number of aqueous crystals increased as hyphema resolved
Iridescent, needle-like crystals were seen floating in the aqueous
Morning glory optic disc anomaly was present
Low-lying detachment of the peripapillary retina was observed
Chronic retinal detachment was found after vitreous hemorrhage resolution

shortlist.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor

shortlist.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
shortlist.why_kept: Association with oxalate crystals in the eye, which could explain the observed crystalline deposits

shortlist.label: Cystinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by cystine crystal accumulation in various tissues, including the eye

shortlist.label: Morning glory syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a morning glory optic disc anomaly, which is a key feature of this condition

shortlist.label: Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous
shortlist.why_kept: Association with retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage, which are present in this case

raw.rationale: The presence of a morning glory optic disc anomaly, which is a characteristic feature of Morning glory syndrome, along with the complications such as retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage, makes it the most likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy
rejected.why: While it involves crystals in the eye, it primarily affects the cornea and retina, not typically associated with morning glory disc anomaly or the specific pattern of retinal detachment seen here.

rejected.label: Primary hyperoxaluria
rejected.why: This condition involves oxalate crystals in the eye but is more commonly associated with systemic symptoms and kidney stones, not specifically with morning glory optic disc anomaly or the described retinal findings.

rejected.label: Cystinosis
rejected.why: Cystinosis can cause crystals in the eye, but it is a systemic lysosomal storage disease with other prominent features not mentioned in the vignette, such as kidney dysfunction and other systemic manifestations.

rejected.label: Persistent hyperplastic primary vitreous
rejected.why: This condition involves abnormal development of the primary vitreous and can cause retinal detachment and vitreous hemorrhage, but it does not typically present with the specific morning glory optic disc anomaly or the iridescent, needle-like crystals in the aqueous humor as described.
